## 2. The twelve rows §6 does not state, and why that is not a gap

A producer map and a manuscript map do not have the same row set, and the difference is
informative rather than embarrassing. `scripts/application/` computes more than the article prints.
The rows above with `—` in the Location column fall into four kinds:

| Kind | Count | Rows | What a reader should conclude |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Run-time assertions** | 3 | `orthogonal_theta()` reproduction; stage-5 reproduction of the stage-2 curve; weighted-layer scale-invariance and bite | Working as intended. These exist to fail a run, not to be read; their only output is stderr and a `stopifnot` |
| **Supplement-only detail under a summary the article does quote** | 6 | the 22 balance covariates; estimator-diagnostic Panels B and C; the robustness comparison block's two rows; design M2 | Working as intended, and it is the article's own float rule: cell-level detail underneath a summary goes to the supplement |
| **Pre-committed machinery whose outcome is visible but whose rule is not stated** | 1 | the V1/V2/V3 verdict | Defensible, but a referee cannot check from the article alone that the rule was fixed in advance. §5.1 states *its* pre-committed criterion in the body; §6 does not state this one |
| **Artifacts the article never names** | 2 | `app_tsp_overlap.tex` (Table S18); `app_tsp_lf_path.pdf` (Figure S5) | **The item here worth an author decision.** See §2.1 |

**Two further rows carry an anchor but not for their headline number**, and the Status column says
so: the `DiffTSP` identity is relied on where §6 defines $\Delta X$ but its $5.33\times10^{-15}$
deviation is not printed, and the weighted layer's unit-weight check is anchored on the $188$ it
shares with the full-sample fit while its $1.11\times10^{-16}$ deviation is not printed. A partial
anchor is recorded as partial rather than promoted to a full one.

### 2.1 Two supplement floats are orphaned from the article

`Table S18` and `Figure S5` occur **zero** times in `main.qmd`, checked on whitespace-flattened text
so that a line break cannot hide a match. Both are real, both are in the supplement, and both are
reachable only by reading the supplement front to back.

- **Table S18 (overlap)** carries the evidence for **A4(i)**, which is a maintained assumption of
  the estimator. §6 discusses A0, A1, A5(i) and the frontier in the body and leaves A4(i) to a table
  it never points at.
- **Figure S5 (Landweber discrepancy paths)** shows five fold solves. §6 says a great deal about
  fold solves reaching the cap and returning their initial condition and never sends the reader to
  the picture of it.

**Recommended, and it is the writer's call, not this map's:** one clause each, in the paragraphs
that already discuss the matching content. Neither is applied here; this map does not edit
`main.qmd`.

## 3. **INV-11 finding — the sixth, and it is reader-visible** — **CLOSED 2026-08-04**

### 3.1 §6 prints $182.5$ where Table S22 prints $182$

- **Prose** (`main.qmd:1932–1934`): "drawing $621$, the expected number of distinct counties in a
  resample of $983$, gives $3$ of $24$ at **a median stopping index of $182.5$** against the full
  sample's $188$."
- **Artifact** (`app_tsp_phi_boot_compare.tex`, Panel A, row "$\hat m_\varphi$: median", column
  $n(1-e^{-1})$): **$182$**.

**The prose is the accurate side.** Read directly out of
`quality_reports/application/app_tsp_phi_band.rds` `$tie`, the 24 stopping indices are

```
1, 1, 1, 87, 102, 114, 126, 127, 136, 147, 168, 179, 186, 214, 234, 244, 250, 250,
397, 580, 864, 1636, 2000, 2000
```

so the 12th and 13th order statistics are $179$ and $186$ and the median is exactly
$(179+186)/2 = \mathbf{182.5}$. The same object confirms the row's other two numbers: $3$ of $24$ at
$\hat m_\varphi=1$, and a full-sample $\hat m_\varphi$ of $188$.

**Why the table disagrees, and it is not a typo.** The formatter is
`int <- function(x) formatC(round(x), format = "d")` at `app_tsp_06_phi_mult.R:702`, and its own
comment two lines above reads:

> `# Rounds rather than truncates: the median of an even number of stopping`
> `# indices can land on a half.`

The comment anticipates the case exactly and then loses it, because R's `round()` is
**round-half-to-even**: `round(182.5)` is `182`, not `183`. So the table prints a value that looks
like a *different* number rather than an obvious rounding, and a reader who checks $182.5$ against
Table S22 finds $182$ half a unit below and cannot tell whether the prose invented the half.

**The same rounding is live at a second cell and is currently harmless.** The $n/2=492$ subsample
median is $149.5$ in the run object and $150$ in the table — half-to-even rounding *up* this time,
because $150$ is even. §6 does not quote it, so no mismatch is reader-visible there. **Any fix
must treat both cells**, or the table becomes internally inconsistent about halves.

**Two clean repairs, and the author chooses:**

1. **Quote the table.** Change $182.5$ to $182$ in `main.qmd:1933`. Cheapest; loses the half.
2. **Print the half.** Make `int()` emit one decimal when `x` is not an integer, so Table S22 shows
   $182.5$ and $149.5$. This is the more honest of the two, since the underlying quantity genuinely
   is a half, and it costs a table rerun only (the run object holds every draw). It would also
   change the printed $150$ to $149.5$, which nothing currently cites.

**Neither is applied here.** This map does not edit `main.qmd`, `supplement.qmd` or any script.

### 3.2 Why the earlier passes did not catch it

Both numbers are individually correct against *some* source: $182.5$ against the run object, $182$
against the shipped table. Any check that asks "does this number appear in an output file" passes on
$182$ and any check that asks "is the prose arithmetically right" passes on $182.5$. The defect is
visible only when the *same quantity* is read out of both at once, which is what a Location column
forces. This is the fifth time on this project that a cross-direction check has found something a
single-direction check could not, and it is the argument for the column.

---

## 4. Defects in this map's own provenance data, found while adding the anchors

The 2026-08-04 header claimed that "every number the application *produces* is traceable to a script
line and an output artifact". Checking the rows against the artifacts while writing the Location
column showed that claim was slightly too strong.

### 4.1 One row named the wrong panel and the wrong line range

The row "Sampling vs cross-fitting share of the standard error" read:

> `app_tsp_common.R` | 470–479 | `app_tsp_estimator_diag.tex` **Panel C**

Both pointers were wrong.

- **The panel is D, not C.** `app_tsp_02_ladder.R:272` writes
  `Panel D: variance decomposition and rate budget`, and the two share rows are written at L275 and
  L277. Panel C is written at L255 and is `scale of the fitted components`, which has no share
  column. The supplement's own Table S21 note gets this right ("Table S20 Panel D prices that
  component at $0.415$"), so the map was the only thing carrying the error.
- **The lines are not 470–479.** `app_tsp_common.R:466–479` is the head of `fit_orthogonal()` — the
  `xeval` default and `make_streams()`. The decomposition is at `app_tsp_common.R:516–524`
  (`se_samp_cl`, `se_cf`, and the `se_cl` they combine into), aggregated to medians at
  `app_tsp_02_ladder.R:221–222`.

Both are corrected in §1. This is the same species as §3.5 of the §5 map: a pointer aimed at the
wrong object, invisible until someone follows it.

### 4.2 Panel C had no row

`app_tsp_estimator_diag.tex` has four panels. The map covered A, B and D-mislabelled-as-C, which
left **Panel C uncovered while appearing to be covered**. Its five rows — the median and max of
$\mathrm{sd}(\Delta\hat\varphi)/\mathrm{sd}(\Delta Y)$ and of
$\mathrm{sd}(\Delta\hat U)/\mathrm{sd}(\Delta Y)$, the $\mathrm{sd}/1.4826\times$MAD ratio of
$\hat\theta_b$, and the count of partitions more than 10 robust scales from the median — are
produced at `app_tsp_02_ladder.R:255–268`. A row is added in §1. Nothing in §6 quotes them.

This is worth stating plainly: **a mislabelled row is worse than a missing one**, because it makes
an audit that greps for panel letters report full coverage.

### 4.3 "14 tuning arms" versus the supplement's "Fifteen tuning arms"

Not an error, recorded so nobody reconciles them in the wrong direction.

`ARMS` at `app_tsp_03_robustness.R:68–88` has **15 entries**, of which the first is `R0` /
`"Baseline"`. The remaining 14 each vary one tuning constant: $X$ coordinate (2), LF step (3),
initial condition (2), $K$ (2), $\rho$ (2), patience (1), cap (1), sample (1). So:

- **this map's "14 tuning arms"** counts the arms that vary something, which is what "tuning arm"
  means;
- **the supplement caption's "Fifteen tuning arms"** (`supplement.qmd:940`) counts the printed
  estimator rows, one of which is the baseline that varies nothing.

Both are defensible and they count different things. The table prints 15 estimator rows and 2
comparison rows either way. **Leave both as they are**; if either moves, the other must.

## 5. Numbers added to §6 after this map was written, verified this pass

Three editing passes ran between the map's 2026-08-02 provenance table and this one. Every number
below was re-read against the artifact named. **None was taken on trust from the change list.**

### 5.1 The F6 fix — §6.5, the per capita income sign flip

All twelve numbers come from `paper/tables/app_tsp_robustness.tex`, rows 7–9 (`Baseline`,
`$X$ in $\mu$g/m$^3$`, `$X$ min--max scaled`). `main.qmd:2104–2108`.

| Number | Where in the artifact | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| $+0.6816$, $-3.6510$, $-3.7961$ | Per capita income, Estimate, rows 7–9 | ✓ exact |
| $0.5111$, $37.3284$, $68.8991$ | Per capita income, (SE), rows 7–9 | ✓ exact |
| $8$ and $9$ of $30$, against $0$ of $30$ | "Fold solves at $\hat m = 1$", rows 8, 9, 7 | ✓ exact, and the order in the prose matches the order of the arms |
| median $\hat m$ of $50$, $14$, against $1{,}083$ | "Median $\hat m$", rows 8, 9, 7 | ✓ exact |

The $30$ denominator is $K\times B = 5\times6$: `N_FOLDS <- 5L` and `N_PART_ROB <- 6L` at
`app_tsp_common.R:180,182`. It is **not** the ladder's $50$, which is $5\times10$ under
`N_PART <- 10L`. That difference is the whole subject of §5.3 below.

### 5.2 The $4.7$ that replaced $4.6$ in §6.5

`main.qmd:2129–2131`. **Recomputed from scratch, two ways, and they agree to four decimals.**

| Route | Value |
|---|---|
| Closed form $(\ln n)^{\kappa}$ at $n=983$, $\kappa=2\mu/(2\mu+1)=0.8$ | $(6.890609)^{0.8} = \mathbf{4.68388}$ |
| Ratio of the two A5(i) branches, $13.0033/2.7762$ | $\mathbf{4.68385}$ |

At one decimal that is **$4.7$**, and the numerator $13.0033$ matches
`app_tsp_feasibility.tex`'s printed $13.0$ at $d_Z=0$ to three figures. The superseded $4.6$ came
from the hedge in a code comment at `app_tsp_01_diagnostics.R:289` ("about 4.6"), which no output
file carries.

**The important half is the clause the fix added, not the digit it changed.** The factor is **not a
constant**: at the $n\approx2.1\times10^{11}$ the same paragraph names it is
$(\ln 2.1\times10^{11})^{0.8} = 13.58$, i.e. about $13.6$. A reader who recomputes at any other $n$
and gets something other than $4.7$ is not finding an error, and §6 now says so in its own voice
("the factor is $(\ln n)^{\kappa}$, not a constant"). Both halves are anchored separately in §1 for
that reason.

### 5.3 The Table S21 note — why Tables S19 and S21 disagree on one coefficient

`supplement.qmd:946–955`. Two independent critics flagged the disagreement; this is the resolution,
and it belongs in a map because the two tables will keep disagreeing.

**The disagreement is real and is not a bug.** Per capita income at the five-control set is:

| Table | Value | Partitions | Fold solves |
|---|---|---|---|
| **S19** (`app_tsp_ladder.tex`, $d_Z=5$) | $0.9603$ | 10 (`N_PART`) | $5\times10 = 50$ |
| **S21** (`app_tsp_robustness.tex`, Baseline) | $0.6816$ | 6 (`N_PART_ROB`) | $5\times6 = 30$ |

Same 983 counties, same five controls, same estimator. The only difference is **tuning constant
C7**, `N_PART <- 10L` / `N_PART_ROB <- 6L` at `app_tsp_common.R:181–182`, documented at C7
(`app_tsp_common.R:100–104`) as raised above the default of 5 "because the pilot showed
cross-fitting noise of the same order as the sampling standard error".

**Verified this pass:**

- $0.6816$ ✓ `app_tsp_robustness.tex` row 7; $0.9603$ ✓ `app_tsp_ladder.tex` row 9, column $d_Z=5$.
- $0.415$ ✓ `app_tsp_estimator_diag.tex` **Panel D**, "Cross-fitting share of SE (median)", column
  $d_Z=5$. The note cites it as "Table S20 Panel D", which is correct — and is the pointer that
  showed §4.1's row to be wrong.
- "**about nine tenths of a standard error**" — the gap is $0.9603-0.6816 = 0.2787$. Against Table
  S19's **robust** SE of $0.3229$ that is $0.863$; against its clustered SE of $0.4031$ it is
  $0.691$; against Table S21's own SE of $0.5111$ it is $0.545$. **The claim reproduces on the
  robust SE of the ladder and on no other denominator.** Recorded because a reader who reaches for
  the nearer standard error gets a different answer and may think the note is wrong.
- The $30$-versus-$50$ fold-solve counts ✓ against both tables, as in §5.1.

The note's closing rule — "Comparisons within this table are like for like; comparisons across the
two tables are not" — is the operative sentence and this map endorses it.

## 7. Reproduction

```bash
Rscript scripts/application/app_tsp_run_all.R
```

Roughly one hour on eight cores for stages 1–4, plus roughly three hours for stage 5.
Stage 2 caches its fits in `quality_reports/application/app_tsp_ladder_ckpt.rds`, keyed on
the estimator sources, the raw data, the tuning constants and the deparsed bodies of the
two driver functions — so editing a table reuses the fits and editing the estimator does
not. Stage 5 caches the same way twice: the three full-sample coordinate arms in
`app_tsp_phi_full_ckpt.rds`, and **one file per bootstrap replication** under
`app_tsp_phi_band_parts/`, so an interrupted run resumes from where it stopped and a table
edit costs nothing.

## 8. Objects a downstream agent can read without rerunning

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `quality_reports/application/app_tsp_diagnostics.rds` | drop table, first stage, balance, overlap, feasibility, probes 1 and 3 |
| `quality_reports/application/app_tsp_ladder.rds` | all four rung fits (including per-partition estimates, Jacobians, LF records), probe 2, $\hat\varphi$, $\hat u$ |
| `quality_reports/application/app_tsp_robustness.rds` | all 14 arms plus the baseline, both comparison estimators, the discrepancy paths |
| `quality_reports/application/app_tsp_ladder_ckpt.rds` | fit cache plus the configuration fingerprint |
| `quality_reports/application/app_tsp_phi_band.rds` | the normalised $\hat\varphi$, the four bootstrap designs with every replication's curve and status, the tabulated grid, the three coordinate arms. **`$tie` is the source of record for the $182.5$ of §3**, and `$bands$C0$q` for the retired 25–75 count recorded in the §5 map §11.1 |
| `quality_reports/application/app_tsp_phi_full_ckpt.rds` | the three full-sample coordinate arms ($\hat\theta$, curve, $\hat m_\varphi$) plus the configuration fingerprint |
| `quality_reports/application/app_tsp_phi_band_parts/` | one `.rds` per bootstrap replication per design: curve, $\hat\theta^*$, status, convergence class, wall time |
| `quality_reports/application/app_tsp_phi_mult.rds` | design M and M2: every replication's curve and status, the assembled bands, the five outcomes for M, C0 and both subsample arms, the verdict and its three components, the layer-verification record. **`$outcomes$subsample$m_med` is $182.5$ and `$outcomes$subsample_eff$m_med` is $149.5$**, both of which the table rounds. **The full M band (all 99 curves and the quantile matrix) is here, so the M figure can be drawn at any time without recomputing anything.** |
| `quality_reports/application/app_tsp_phi_mult_parts/` | one `.rds` per multiplier replication per design: curve, $\hat m_\varphi$, status, convergence class, weight s.d., Kish $n_{\text{eff}}$, wall time |
| `quality_reports/application/app_tsp_phi_mult_valid.rds` | the weighted layer's verification against the untouched estimator (unit-weight, scale-invariance and bite deviations) |
| `quality_reports/application/app_tsp_phi_mult_sub_ckpt.rds` | the 24 information-matched ($n/2$) without-replacement subsample solves |

## 9. What the $\hat\varphi$ band is

**An illustrative variability band, not a confidence set**, following the convention of
Centorrino, Fève and Florens (2025, *J. Econometrics*), Figure 4 note, for the same
estimator on the same equation: *"The confidence intervals for the nonparametric estimator
are presented only to illustrate its variability but should not be considered valid."*
No coverage is claimed and none is computed. The full design rationale — what is
resampled, why the stopping index is re-selected, how failures are counted — is in the
header of `scripts/application/app_tsp_05_phi_band.R`.

## 10. Claims deliberately **not** made about §6

| Non-claim | Why |
|---|---|
| "The application validates the estimator" | §6's own closing sentence is that the application "illustrates the procedure on a design the method was built for; it does not demonstrate that the asymptotics bind at this sample size". At $n=983$ the object that describes the estimator is `cor:ratefloor`, not `thm:rootn`, and §6 says so |
| "The band shows the hedonic gradient is signed" | The envelope contains zero at all eleven tabulated levels and at every point of the 60-point grid. §6 draws no inference from the widths **in either direction** and this map does not add one |
| "A1 survives the probes" | Probe 2 rejects at four of five stratifications. §6 reports the rejection together with its confound (the residual is fitted by an estimator whose stopping index reaches the cap on 8 to 10 of 50 fold solves) and states that nothing on disk separates the two |
| "The imputed designation is validated by `cropper2023`" | That paper reports a reassuring *comparison* and leaves open which definition guided policy; §6 also states the monitor-siting channel by which the non-differential condition could fail, and concludes that nothing in their evidence or ours settles it |
| "The curve's magnitudes are features of the data" | They are conditional on tuning constant C2. §6 says so in its own voice, and the two alternative coordinates move the normalised curve by up to $0.515$, which is 62 per cent of its own range |
| "The two tight bands in Panel C are the robust ones" | They are the arms whose iteration stopped far short of the baseline's $188$: $\hat m_\varphi=1$ in $\mu$g/m$^3$ and $62$ in min–max. §6 states the inversion explicitly. **Corrected 2026-08-05:** this row previously read "the arms in which the estimator never iterated", which its own numbers refute — $62$ is not never. §6 no longer offers early stopping as the mechanism either, since Panel B's $\theta$-re-estimation block halves the band with no coordinate change |

**§6.2's probe-2 prose and `paper/tables/app_tsp_misclass.tex` disagree about whether the paper's
own test of A1 rejects.** They disagree in direction, not in rounding.

| | Values | Provenance |
|---|---|---|
| §6.2 prose | $p=0.109$, $0.132$, $0.594$, $0.072$, $0.075$; "Nothing rejects at conventional levels" | matches `quality_reports/decisions/alternative-applications.md`, whose withdrawal note is dated **2026-08-07** |
| `app_tsp_misclass.tex` probe-2 block, on disk | ten rows, $p=0.000$, $0.015$, $0.014$, $0.000$, $0.003$, $0.000$, $0.000$, $0.044$, $0.000$, $0.002$ | file mtime **2026-08-08 08:07**, written by `app_tsp_02_ladder.R` |
| this map's own row 85 | $0.033$, $0.000$, $0.003$, $0.003$, $0.638$ | a **third** vintage, the pre-correction one |

Three vintages, no two equal, describing one probe. The table is the **newest** of the three, so
the prose is the stale party and not the table, which is the opposite of the usual direction here.

What changed on 2026-08-08 is structural and not a rerun of the same statistic:
`app_tsp_02_ladder.R` now computes **two** hypotheses per stratification, the predecessor's
unconditional contrast and A1's conditional one, giving ten rows where the prose describes five.
Reading the block in pairs, the A1 rows are $p=0.015$, $0.000$, $0.000$, $0.044$, $0.002$ — all
rejecting at five per cent. The script also carries `PROBE2_A1_VALID`, which marks **four of the
five** stratifications size-invalid because the stratum tracks $\Delta Z$; the printed table carries
no such flag and the prose does not mention it. The two rows of each pair print under identical
row labels with different numbers, which is a second, independent defect in that table.

**Why this pass did not repair it.** The repair is not a prose edit. Either the prose is retyped
against the ten-row table, which changes §6.2's verdict on A1 from "nothing rejects" to "the A1
reading rejects at all five, four of them at a size-invalid stratification", or the table is
regenerated at whatever specification the 2026-08-07 record describes. Both are the coder's call
and both change what the section concludes. Writing five numbers over ten without knowing which
specification is intended would be the defect this project keeps producing, one directory over.

**What this pass did do.** §7's summary of the probe no longer asserts a direction. It previously
read "does not reject at any of the five stratifications, the smallest $p$-value being $0.072$",
which repeats the contested numbers in a second section; it now says only that a test run on a
noisier fitted residual is uninformative whichever way it comes out, and points at
\cref{sec:app-localise} as the section's evidence about A1 — which is what
`tab:app-misclass`'s own note already says. **§6.2's prose is untouched and the mismatch is live.**

**Row 85 of §1 above is stale in its verification column** and is left as written, with this
section as the correction of record, so that the three vintages stay visible rather than being
flattened into a fourth.

> read from `app_tsp_phi_band.rds` rather than from a printed table, so they were not checkable in
> this pass — but they describe a curve whose two printed endpoints have both changed sign, and they
> should be assumed stale until re-derived.
>
> **The two arithmetic checks recorded at the end of this subsection do not survive either.** "The
> six non-exclusions" was $11-5=6$; the count is now $1$, so the arithmetic is $11-1=10$. "The two
> that did not cannot be carrying the band" reasoned from $2$ degenerate replications inside a
> $5$th–$95$th trim of $99$; there are now $0$.

>
> **The 2026-08-26 banner named §13.2 because §13.2 is where the sign flip was found. That is the

## 14. §6.2's probe-2 passage and §7's summary of it, retyped 2026-08-11 by the Writer

**This section closes §12 and supersedes §13.1.** Both are left as written.

**The author's ruling that governs this pass.** §6 may not assert that A1 is rejected, and may not
assert that nothing rejects either. The exercise cannot settle A1: $\Delta\hat U$ is the residual of
a fit made *under* A1, and block (b)'s reference law is drawn from $\hat\varrho$, so its $p$-values
are joint against A1 and the specification of the propensity. **The passage reports the table and
declines the inference.** No substitute conclusion was manufactured for the one withdrawn.

### 14.3 What the passage now claims, and what it explicitly declines to claim

**Claims.**

1. Block (a) — the predecessor's unconditional restriction $\Delta U\upmodels W$ — is rejected at
   every stratification, and **that is a result the paper needs**: it is why the conditional form of
   A1 is imposed at all. Size is not at stake in that block.
2. A rejection in block (a) is what A1 itself predicts once $\varrho(\Delta Z)$ varies inside a
   stratum, so the evidence there runs against the unconditional restriction and **not** against the
   conditional one.
3. Block (b) — A1's restriction — rejects at five per cent at all five stratifications, and four of
   the five rows do not have nominal size, for a stated mechanical reason.
4. The one size-valid row is the baseline-particulate quartile, and it carries the largest statistic
   in the block.
5. Through an earlier draft the probe formed only the unconditional contrast and the paper reported
   it as a test of A1. **The record kept is that the label was wrong, not that the numbers were.**

**Declines.**

1. Does **not** claim A1 is rejected.
2. Does **not** claim nothing rejects.
3. Does **not** offer a replacement verdict of any kind. The closing sentence is "We report the
   block and decline to read A1 off it in either direction."
4. Does **not** claim the corrected estimator is noisier, or that a power loss explains anything.
   That argument is deleted, not weakened.
5. Does **not** rank §6.3 above probe 2. See §14.5.

### 14.4 The table note (INV-1)

The note previously described probe 2 as **one** permutation test with a binary $W$-contrast, which
covered five of the ten printed rows and left the fourth column undefined. It now: describes both
blocks and their two null laws; defines "Valid size" as whether the block-(b) reading attains its
nominal level at that stratification, judged by the size simulation, with the mechanism and the
governing magnitude ("about seven times in ten against a nominal five per cent"); says why the
column is `--` on the block-(a) rows; keeps the standing caveat, now stated for **both** reference
distributions; and adds `scripts/simulations/sim_probe2_size.R` to the Sources line.

### 14.5 Two claims that were **removed** rather than corrected, and why

1. **The note's "the cell-by-cell diagnostic of \cref{sec:app-localise} supersedes probe 2 as this
   paper's evidence about A1 … rather than on either contaminated residual."** The phrase "either
   contaminated residual" is stale — there is one residual now, from the corrected conditional fit,
   and both blocks run on it. And under the ruling that the exercise cannot settle A1, asserting
   that §6.3 *is* the paper's evidence about A1 would pre-empt the blocked §6.3 ruling in the wrong
   direction. Replaced with a neutral pointer: §6.3 "reports a separate cell-by-cell diagnostic on
   the four-category fit, which returns an attribution rather than a verdict."
2. **§7's "It is the cell-by-cell diagnostic and not that probe that carries this paper's evidence
   about A1."** Same reason. Dropped, not softened; §7's paragraph above it already describes the
   attribution in full, so nothing is lost. **§7's localisation paragraph itself was not touched.**

### 14.7 A build regression this pass created and closed in the same pass

Adding `\citet{mastentorgovitsky2014}` put **two undefined citations** into the printed bibliography
(`Citation 'masten2016' undefined`, pages 123 and 129) and drove biblatex to the render script's
9-run ceiling. Cause: the `mastentorgovitsky2014` entry's own `note` field contains
`\textcite{masten2016}`, which does not resolve unless the published note is also in the
bibliography. The two entries are **not** interchangeable — the bib's own header records that the
Chay–Greenstone application survives only in the 2014 working paper — so the fix is `\nocite{masten2016}`,
carried with a comment at the citation site, and **not** re-pointing the `\citet`. Rebuild after the
fix: exit 0, 130 pages, zero undefined refs, zero unresolved cites, no run-ceiling warning.

§13.1 flagged that the iteration-cap sentence was factually correct while **the argument around it
was gone**, and asked for an author ruling. The ruling arrived and the argument was deleted. The cap
numbers ($0$ of $50$; $8$, $15$, $34$ of $50$) no longer appear in §6.2 or §7. They remain correct
and remain printed in `app_tsp_estimator_diag.tex` Panel A and in the supplement; §6.6 continues to
use them for what they actually diagnose.

**⚠ A SECOND LIVE INV-11 EXPOSURE, FOUND WHILE VERIFYING, INSIDE BLOCKED SCOPE, NOT REPAIRED.**
The brief did not anticipate this one, and it is the same species as §12 — prose describing a
superseded vintage of an artifact that has since been regenerated.

`scripts/application/app_tsp_common.R:296–303` records that `B_LOCALISE` was **raised from $400$ to
$2{,}000$ on 2026-08-11** because at $400$ the localisation statistic was **floor-censored**: both
chronic cells returned exactly $1/401=0.00249$, i.e. no null draw reached the observed norm, and
§6.3 printed those as two distinct values and read a monotone ordering off them. The script's own
comment is explicit that *"there is no ordering to read at the floor."*
**The diagnostic has since been re-run**, and `quality_reports/sim/localise_four_cell.md` (header:
"$2{,}000$ null draws") now prints numbers §6.3 does not carry:

| Cell | §6.3 / §7 / §1 prose | `localise_four_cell.md`, in-sample $\hat\varrho$ | cross-fitted $\hat\varrho$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| bad-day only | $p=0.062$ | $0.0745$ | $0.0770$ |
| annual-mean only | $p=0.005$ | $0.0015$ | $0.0015$ |
| both triggers | $p=0.003$ | $0.0025$ | $0.0015$ |
| moment norms / null medians | $2.2$, $3.2$, $4.4$ | $2.02$, $3.41$, $3.61$ (recomputed from the $\|M_l\|$ and null-median columns) | — |
| reference draws | "$400$ draws" | $2{,}000$ | — |

**Six numbers and one count, in five blocked places**: §6.3, §7's localisation paragraph, §1's
fourth contribution item, the abstract, and the structure comment at the head of `main.qmd`.

**One of them is not a rounding move.** §6.3 reads the two chronic $p$-values as $0.005$ then
$0.003$, so that the both-triggers cell is the smaller. At $B=2{,}000$ the in-sample column has
annual-mean at $0.0015$ **below** both-triggers at $0.0025$, and the cross-fitted column ties them.
The *conclusion* §6.3 draws — that the both-triggers cell carries the largest violation — survives,
because it rests on the moment-norm ratio ($3.61$ is still the largest) and not on the $p$-values;
but the ordering as stated in $p$ does not.

**Three numbers in §6.3 were checked and do hold**: $\min_l\hat\varrho_l=0.0115$,
$\lambda_{\min}(\hat\Omega)=0.0113$ against $\varepsilon_\varrho/\mathsf L=0.0029$.

### 15.3 Sentences MOVED rather than cut

Three sentences of the deleted §6.4 are limitations of the *estimator* rather than of the withdrawn
empirical claim, and the brief directed that such sentences be folded into the bootstrap beat. They
open §6.3 in the manuscript now:

1. Uniform bands need a source condition written at an adjoint and completeness of the instrument;
   the operator equation is nonlinear so there is no adjoint, and a four-valued $W$ delivers
   completeness no more than a two-valued one (`severini2006`, `babiiflorens2025`).
2. `chen2012b` reaches nonlinearly ill-posed conditional moment models but indexes its sets by a
   *deterministic* sieve dimension, whereas `def:lfstep`'s index is the random stopping time of a
   discrepancy rule.
3. The companion-paper convention (`centorrinofeveflorens2019`) and the sentence saying what the band
   is not.

The deleted subsection's `monardnicklpaternain2021` sentence was **not** moved: §7's fifth
future-work item already carries it verbatim, and that item is untouched.

### 16.3 Claims WITHDRAWN rather than renumbered

These are gone from `main.qmd`. Each was not merely stale; the quantity it rested on no longer
discriminates, so replacing the number would have preserved a defective inference.

1. **"The width of the band is therefore a property of the estimator at this effective sample
   size, and not an artefact of how the sample is resampled."** (was `main.qmd:2171-2173`, in
   bold.) The entire argument ran through the stopping index: $7$ of $99$ against $2$ of $99$ at
   $\hat m_\varphi=1$, $0$ of $24$ and $2$ of $24$ in the subsamples, a median index of $19.5$
   against $28$. Under `TAU_DP = 0` **every one of those quantities is $60$**, so the comparison
   has no axis. `app_tsp_phi_mult.rds` records `verdict = NA` with
   `verdict_axis_degenerate = TRUE` and all three criteria `TRUE` by construction. The paragraph
   now reports what each scheme produced and states that no preference is claimed.
2. **"Information moves the stopping index where duplication does not."** Same cause. There is
   no measured movement in the stopping index under any scheme.
3. **"$2$ replications stopped at the first iteration ... and none ran to the cap"**, and the
   arithmetic that followed it (the $97$-of-$99$ argument, and the claim that two replications
   cannot set either edge of a $5$–$95$ envelope). All $99$ run to the cap; none can stop at $1$.
   The figure note's "only $2$ of those $99$ replications stopped at the first iteration" went
   with it.
4. **"the largest move, manufacturing employment at $0.69$, sits on a coefficient that is under
   two standard errors from zero in both."** The largest move is now the high-school share, and
   that coefficient is $2.80$ clustered standard errors from zero at $\mathsf L=4$, so the old
   rationale does not transfer. Replaced by a claim that is true of the new argmax: it keeps its
   sign and stays inside either column's interval.
5. **"It does not make the band valid, which remains barred for the reason given above: the
   regularisation index is a random stopping time."** False *of these runs* — the index is fixed
   at $\bar m$. The subsection's opening paragraph now says so explicitly and re-bases the
   obstruction on the two that do bind (no adjoint under nonlinearity; no completeness from a
   discrete $W$).
6. **"so the only difference between the two columns is the instrument's cardinality and what
   that does to the propensity"**, at both `tab:app-theta`'s introduction and its note. The
   iteration cap moves with $\mathsf L$ as well ($60$ against $15$), so the columns are not a
   clean one-factor contrast. Found this pass; not in the brief.

### 16.5 A precision convention adopted this pass, and why

Every band width stated in §6 is the **difference of the two endpoints `app_tsp_phi.tex` and
`app_tsp_phi_mult.tex` print**, not the rounded difference of the underlying doubles. These
differ in one place: the C0 width at the 5th percentile is $0.063366$, which rounds to $0.0634$,
while $0.0444-(-0.0189)=0.0633$. **$0.0633$ is the value in the text**, so a reader subtracting
the printed endpoints reproduces every width in the subsection exactly. The brief quoted
$0.0634$; the difference is this convention and not a disagreement about the artifact.

### 16.6 What this pass did NOT touch

- **`scripts/`, `paper/tables/`, `supplement.qmd`, `quality_reports/theory/`** — out of scope
  by the brief, and untouched.
- **The boundary-adjustment question** — out of scope by the brief. §6 says nothing about it in
  either direction, before or after this pass.
- **The $\mathsf L=3$ / $\mathsf L=4$ simulation tables.** `sim_multinomial_precision.tex`,
  `_onestep`, `_phistop`, `_phifit`, `_phiplugin`, `_phicost`, `_dgpvalid`, `_rootn`,
  `_rootn_misspec` and `_tau` are on disk and are `\input` by **neither** document. Not placed;
  that is the next pass.
- **`app_tsp_phi_mult.tex` and `app_tsp_phi_mult.pdf`** are on disk and `\input` by no document.
  §6 reads the multiplier arm's summary out of Table S22, which *is* printed, and reads the
  three tail widths of row 16.44 out of the unprinted table. **A reader can check the tail
  reversal on the resample side only.** Whether the multiplier table joins the supplement is an
  author decision; it was not taken here.
- **§7's "the regularisation index of `def:lfstep` is the random stopping time of a discrepancy
  rule"** (`main.qmd:2371` region). Left as written: it is a statement about the *definition*,
  which does carry a discrepancy branch, and it is not falsified by §6's runs disabling that
  branch. §6 now states the disabling explicitly, so the two are compatible — but they describe
  the same index in two different registers, and an author ruling on whether §7 should carry the
  same qualification is owed.

`supplement.qmd` was not edited. Table numbering in the article is unchanged by this pass
(8/9/10 = firststage / theta / phi; Figure 4 = `fig:app-phi`), so §15.9's ledger is unaffected.

(`supplement.qmd:1019`) gloss a row called "No NPIV estimate produced", which

## 17. §6 re-sourced against the boundary-adjusted, one-factor tables — 2026-08-15, by the Writer

**What forced the pass.** Two changes to the estimator since §16 moved every number in beats 2
and 3. (a) The $x$-direction kernel gained the renormalisation
$C_{h_x}(x-X)/\int_{\mathcal X}C_{h_x}(y-X)\,dy$, so the $j=0$ truncated moment is exactly one at
every design point; before it, the application implemented **no** boundary adjustment while the
simulation that verifies `thm:rootn` implemented this one, i.e. §5 verified one estimator and §6
shipped another. (b) `tab:app-theta`'s cardinality comparison was made a **one-factor** contrast:
both columns now run at $\varepsilon_\varrho=0.01$ **and** $\bar m=60$, where the second column
previously ran at the $\bar m=15$ its own cardinality sets.

**Read from the tables, not from §16's rows.** Every value below was read out of
`paper/tables/*.tex` or, for grid-level facts the tables do not print, recomputed from
`quality_reports/application/app_tsp_phi_band.rds` in this pass. §16's rows for beats 2 and 3 are
superseded wholesale and are not individually struck.

> **SUPERSEDED 2026-08-20 — DO NOT READ §17.1 OR §17.2 AS LIVE.** Four §6 tables were regenerated
> after this section was written. The values below described the artifacts of 2026-08-15 and no
> longer describe the shipped ones: the cap contrast, the six per-coordinate gaps, the sign
> exception, the N1 defect row, and the one-factor $\hat\varphi$ gap are all dead. Kept as trail,
> not struck. **Live values: §23.2.**

### 17.3 The fourth claim, and which comparison §6 now means

§6 previously read the two cardinalities' curves as agreeing closely. That reading survives only in
the **two-factor** comparison, where the cap moves with the cardinality: sup $0.0131$, RMS $0.62$
band standard deviations. It is an artefact of two effects that nearly cancel. Under one factor,
both arms at $\bar m=60$, the sup gap is $0.0479$ and the RMS gap $1.71$ band sd, **3.6 times
larger**; and the cap alone at $\mathsf L=2$ moves the curve by $0.0569$, which is *larger than the
cardinality gap it is being netted against*. `app_tsp_localise_theta_tied.tex` shows the same
cancellation in $\hat\theta$: the two contrasts are opposite in sign at five of six coordinates.

**§6 now means the one-factor comparison throughout**, reports it, names the two-factor number, and
says it measures nothing. `tab:app-theta` and `tab:app-theta-cap` are the two floats that make the
decomposition checkable.

### 17.5 The localisation reinstatement, and what it does not claim

The 2026-08-11 withdrawal was correct against the run it described. At that vintage the two cells it
ranked were separated by two null draws out of two thousand against a Monte Carlo standard error of
$0.0011$. The current run separates them by eleven: exceedance counts $53$, $12$, $1$ at $B=2{,}000$,
Monte Carlo standard errors $0.0036$, $0.0018$, $0.0007$. §6 therefore reports the three cells and
**still draws no ordering from them**, because `prp:localise`(iii) makes consistency necessary and
not sufficient for A1 and the false-negative rate of the attribution is unpriced. Cell 3 prints as
$p<0.001$ and not as a number: $(1+1)/(2000+1)$ is the smallest value the rule can return, so a
smaller figure would describe $B$ and not the data.

### 17.6 The N1 diagnostic — what it is and what it is not

`cor:centarity` (new in §2, 2026-08-15) makes N1 a condition on a $p\times(\mathsf L-1)$ matrix,
hence $p(\mathsf L-1)$ scalar conditions, and (T-2) assumes it at $L_\star$. **The estimator does
not impose it**: `eval_lambda()` anchors at $u=-\infty$ and `eval_moment()` then subtracts the
*unconditional* column mean per $(j,l)$, which is a constant and not a function of $\Delta Z$.
Because projecting on a basis containing an intercept preserves sample means, the reported figure is
the **minimal** N1 defect over the whole class of constant anchors.

Two readings are declined in the manuscript and are recorded here so they are not later reinstated:

1. **Not evidence of absence.** At $n=983$ the defect is not resolvable from zero ($p=0.120$
   entrywise at $\mathsf L=4$), so the non-rejection is a statement about power.
2. **No moment-level check could have caught it.** $E[\widetilde W_l\hat L_{jl}\mid\Delta Z]=0$
   holds automatically under A1 *whatever the anchor is*, because $\widetilde W$ is conditionally
   centred and $\hat L(\Delta U)$ is conditionally independent of $W$. The row
   "Contracted, $\varpi_w\widetilde W$" is printed precisely so that an orthogonal-looking moment
   cannot be read as evidence for N1; it is the smallest of the three statistics at every arm.

Inference in §6 is **conditional on N1**, and `prp:orthog`(iii) prices its failure in the propensity
direction at the full rate $r_n$, undamped. §5's cardinality arm measures what that costs in a
design where the same defect is present by declaration.

### 17.8 Two corrections made to this pass's own draft, recorded so they are not repeated

1. **The N1 table's basis.** A first draft of `tab:app-n1`'s note said the conditional mean was
   fitted on a *linear* basis. It is **quadratic, rank 21** — `PRIMARY <- "quadratic"` in
   `app_tsp_10_n1_anchor.R`, chosen as the basis that spans the estimator's own propensity index.
   The linear-basis figures are in the `.rds` and are smaller (entrywise defect $0.067$ against
   $0.306$); using them would have understated the defect.
2. **What the "Raw" column is.** The same draft said it was the statistic *before* the estimator's
   unconditional sweep. It is not: the pre-sweep statistic is a separate `kind`
   (`entrywise_raw`, median $2.96$) and is **not printed**. "Raw" is the post-sweep projection
   norm, which at rank 21 is overfitting-dominated and is reported only against its own permutation
   floor. The columns that carry the claim are "Debiased" and "$95\%$ upper".
3. **"Smaller on every statistic."** Withdrawn: the $\mathsf L=2$ arms are *larger* than
   $\mathsf L=4$ on the $95\%$ upper bound of the third row, the
   $\varpi_w\widetilde W$ contraction ($0.0621$ and $0.0644$ against $0.0600$). The manuscript now
   compares only on the statistic (T-2) asks for, the entrywise maximum.

### 21.7 A layout defect found while verifying, which would have silently deleted the repair

**The repaired note did not fit, and every automated check said it did.** `sidewaystable` boxes its
content and rotates it; content past the page runs off the paper edge and is simply absent from the
PDF. There is **no** `Overfull \vbox`, no `Float too large`, and `render.sh` exits 0 and reports
zero errors, zero undefined refs, zero unresolved cites. **at the 2026-08-25 build there is ONE `Float too large` warning, S22's; S19 became a portrait `longtable`.** Through 2026-08-24 the two `Float too large` warnings this
document does emit belong to S19 and S22, so their absence at S21 proves nothing.

The first repair draft lost its last two and a half lines — **the entire `Source:` line**, an INV-1
violation — while the render reported clean. Measured natural heights of the whole `threeparttable`,
note included, against the real wall (the 612pt paper edge, *not* `\textwidth` = 469.8pt, which
this float already overruns by design):

| Version | `\tabcolsep` | Height | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre-repair note | 4pt | $585.1$pt | fit, ~27pt spare |
| first repair draft | 4pt | $680.8$pt | clipped, lost the Source line |
| repaired note | 4pt | $621.1$pt | clipped by one line |
| **repaired note (shipped)** | **6pt** | **$597.1$pt** | **fits, 14.9pt spare** |

**The fix spends unused width to buy height, so no verified claim had to be cut.** `threeparttable`
sets the tablenotes to the *width of the table*, so widening the table widens the note's measure and
costs it lines. The file's own header measured 68pt of unused rotated width; at `\tabcolsep` 6pt the
table is 622.0pt, still 28pt inside the 650.4pt rotated budget, and the float drops 24.0pt. Row
heights are unaffected by column separation, so all 24pt come out of the note. Confirmed no new
overfull box at 6pt; the overfull `\hbox`es in the log are math displays in the theory corpus on
pp. 291–304.

**Trimming words did not help, and this is the trap.** Overflow is quantised in whole lines, so two
successive rounds of shortening changed nothing visible while the note stayed one line over. Only
retiring a line, or widening the measure, moves it.

**Regression canary, now recorded in `supplement.qmd` above the float.** The note's last token is
its own test:

```
pdftotext -f 34 -l 34 paper/qmd/_output/supplement.pdf - | grep 'app_tsp_robustness.rds'
```

Empty output means the note is over budget. This is the only check that catches it — the log will
not.

### 23.1 Claim REVERSALS — sentences rewritten, not renumbered

A reversal is a sentence whose *argument* fails at the new value, not merely its digits. Five were
found; the writer-critic named two of them.

|---|---|---|
| "one coordinate moves by more than three fifths of a standard error and the rest by less than half of one" | The largest gap is **income at $0.520$**; nothing reaches three fifths, and *two* coordinates exceed a quarter | "no coordinate moves by as much as $0.53$ of a standard error and four of the six move by less than a quarter of one" |
| "nearly four times the next coordinate, which is the unemployment rate at $0.0560$" | The next coordinate is **manufacturing employment at $0.1334$** and the ratio is **$1.45$**, not four. ## 25. The 2026-08-23 §6 pass, mapped; and the verification-debt corrections — 2026-08-23

**Why this section exists.** The 2026-08-23 pass edited §6 and wrote no map. Everything below the
scope line was reconstructed from the shipped `main.qmd`, the generated `.tex` artifacts and
`main.aux` — never from a source comment, and never from a row of this map, §16 being the standing
proof of why. The pass's real find had been sitting unrecorded: §6 claimed an elasticity inside
Chay and Greenstone's range that is not inside it.

**Scope.** §6.1's linear benchmark; the article's supplement-float pointer; four rotated-float
geometry certificates; four numbers in §6 whose printed precision their own sources do not carry;
and three anchors in this map that stopped matching `main.qmd`. Nothing under `scripts/` except
`scripts/render-paper/render.sh`, and nothing under `quality_reports/theory/`.

### 25.1 The elasticity repair — the find the pass did not record

`main.qmd` used to say the implied elasticity sat **“squarely in Chay and Greenstone’s range”** and
that the reduced form **“behaves as the literature reports.”** It does not sit inside that range.

| Quantity | Source | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Linear IV coefficient on $\Delta X$, headline set $d_Z=5$ | `app_tsp_firststage.tex` L21, col. 2 | $-5.519\times10^{-3}$ |
| 1970 mean TSP | `app_tsp_sumstats.tex` L6 | $66.018\,\mu$g/m$^3$ |
| Implied elasticity at that mean | product of the two | $-0.36435\to-0.364$ |
| `chay2005`'s reported range | `\citet{chay2005}`, linear IV on this design | $-0.20$ to $-0.35$ |
| Distance past the more negative end of that range | $-0.36435-(-0.35)$ | $-0.01435\to0.014$ |

The repaired sentence states the distance and the direction rather than a containment: *“It sits
just past the more negative end of that range, by $0.014$, and reproduces its sign and its order of
magnitude rather than falling inside it.”* Anchor: `It sits just past the more negative end of that
range, by $0.014$,` — unique in `main.qmd`.

**This is why the row at the head of this map had two dead anchors.** Both retired strings were the
withdrawn claim; the row that cited them kept citing them. Repointed in place, with the reason,
under *Reduced form of $\Delta Y$ on $W$*.

### 25.2 The article's supplement-float pointer: a roll became a range

§6's header comment named the supplement's floats as a roll of ten descriptions, S15–S24, and the
supplement now carries S1–S27 and Figures S1–S5. Verified against `supplement.aux`: 27 `tab:supp`
labels and 5 `fig:supp` labels. The roll was replaced by the range in the 2026-08-23 pass; recorded
here because a roll goes stale one float at a time and this map is where that should be countable.

## 26. The 2026-08-24 S23 conversion, mapped — written 2026-08-24, by the Writer

**Why this section exists at all.** The conversion ran on 2026-08-24 and produced **no entry in
either claim-source map**; both ended 2026-08-23. It is recorded now, retrospectively, and the gap
is stated rather than papered over: for one day the supplement's most consequential float change of
the week existed only in a `.qmd` comment. §25.5 of this map closed with the S23 defect **Open**,
explicitly deferred to the author's ruling. The ruling came, the conversion was made, and the map
was not reopened — which is the deferral half of the failure class §24 of the §5 map documents.

### 26.1 What was wrong, and what was done

`tab:supp-app-phimult` (S23), a `sidewaystable`, was **shipping with no caption and no number.**
`rotating.sty`'s `\end@rotfloat` zeroes the float box's `\wd`, `\ht` and `\dp` and sets
`\hbox to\columnwidth{\hss <box>\hss}`; the `\hss` on both sides lets the box overrun **silently** —
no `Overfull \hbox`, no `Float too large`, exit code 0. The wall is `\paperwidth` = 614.295pt, and
because the box is centred the overrun sheds at **both ends at once**: 15.94pt through, 10.97pt at
the head and 4.97pt at the tail. The head carries the caption, the tail carries the note's Source
line. Both were lost. `supplement.aux` still carried
`\newlabel{tab:supp-app-phimult}{{S23}…}`, so every `\cref` resolved and the log stayed clean —
the printed numbering ran **S22, S24**.

**Converted to `landscape` + `longtable`, author-ruled.** A `longtable` that outruns the measure
reports `Overfull \hbox … in alignment`; one that outruns the page **breaks**. Neither is silent
and neither loses printed text, so the conversion replaces a wall that clips with a measure that
cannot.

### 26.2 Verified at the 2026-08-24 build

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Supplement caption census, `Table S`$n$`:` on the rendered PDF | **S1–S27, no gap.** The S23 gap recorded at §25.5 is closed |
| Article caption census | Tables 1–26, no gap |
| S23 head canary — the caption prints | `"Table S23: The variability band under multiplier weights, and the design that produced it"`, 1 hit |
| S23 tail canary — the note's last token prints | `app_tsp_phi_mult.tex`, 1 hit |
| `supplement.log`, `Float too large` | **ONE warning at the 2026-08-25 build, S22 alone** — S19 converted to a portrait `longtable`. Through 2026-08-24: two, S19 and S22. **Neither was ever S23** |

Both canaries returned **0** on 2026-08-23 and return **1** now. That is the finding: the two ends
that were being shed are both on the sheet.

> **A note on the head canary, so it is not misread against its sibling.** §23.6 of the §5 map
> requires `tab:sim-stopping`'s head canary to return **2**, because its `(continued)` header
> reprints the caption and a `grep -c` would answer 1 on a clipped caption that page 2 alone
> reprinted. S23's returns **1**, and that is correct here rather than a failure: this table does
> not carry a continuation header reprinting its caption. The two canaries have different expected
> values for a structural reason, and each is only meaningful against its own float. **Do not
> normalise them to each other.**

### 28.8 One change to shared tooling, and it is a bug fix rather than a feature

`scripts/render-paper/render.sh`'s `captions()` read
`re.finditer(rf"{kind} (S?)(\d+): (.{{0,90}})", text)`, which consumes the label **plus 90
characters**. `finditer` does not overlap, so **a caption printed within 90 characters of the
previous one was swallowed and never entered the dictionary.** It fired for the first time on this
pass: `tab:app-phi` landed as S43 with `tab:supp-app-bootcompare` at S44 **seventy-eight characters
later** in the extracted text, and *"Table S44 of the supplement"* was reported
**`!! NOT PRINTED (out of range)`** while the caption census counted S1..S49 with no gaps and the
float printed perfectly well.

The match now consumes the label alone and slices afterwards, splitting at the next caption label.
**It can only make the resolver see more captions, never fewer, so it cannot mask a real
out-of-range pointer**, and it would have changed no earlier result. Recorded here and flagged in the
return message because it is shared infrastructure: `render.sh` was explicitly **not** modified in
§27, and the author can revert it at the cost of one standing false alarm.

  of the section, and several clauses in them are prior repairs. Trimming them is the largest single
  saving still available and it is put to the author rather than taken here.
- **The supplement's $56$ overfull `\hbox`es are not reduced**, and none of its three
  *Float too large* warnings crosses the paper edge.
- **The three `eq:kernelcompare` danglers are untouched**, as pre-existing and out of scope.
- **The introduction is the third cut and is not begun.** The article is now $19{,}001$ raw source
  words against an OBES target of about $11{,}000$ all in.

#### 28.13.3 Kept at the float against the budget, and why

Four items cost words and were kept. Two because a reader of the float **alone** would be misled
without them, and two by standing ruling.

1. **`tab:app-localise` — the reference distribution "redraws $W$ from the fitted multinomial ...
   and not a permutation".** A permutation would break the $\Delta Z$-conditioning as well, so it
   tests a different and stronger hypothesis; without the clause the $p$-column is read against the
   wrong null. Kept in compressed form ($\approx25$ words against $\approx38$).
2. **`fig:app-phi` — "not confidence sets; no coverage is claimed for them and none is computed".**
   Two shaded envelopes with no such sentence are read as coverage, and this figure travels in talks
   apart from its section. Kept verbatim; the budget was taken from the rug and the axis sentences.
3. **`tab:app-theta` — the five differenced controls by name.** INV-1's "key variables"; author
   ruling, this pass. Cost $\approx16$ words. Four of the five duplicate the printed row stubs, but
   "High school" is ambiguous without the gloss "the share with a high-school education".
4. **`tab:app-theta` — the `app_tsp_boundary.tex` ablation path.** That file is orphaned **on
   purpose** and two comments in `supplement.qmd` (at S25 and at the boundary-layer table) pin their
   own departure to the ruling that the ablation is "cited by path in `tab:app-theta`'s notes".
   Moving it would have made both of those stale — the defect species this project keeps repairing.
   Cost $\approx14$ words.

`tab:app-theta` therefore lands at $135$ rather than $\approx120$, and **$30$ of those $135$ words
are items 3 and 4.** `tab:app-localise` lands at $140$ because it defines eight columns plus a
four-row sensitivity block and carries item 1. Both overshoots are stated rather than absorbed.

**One compression is also a precision gain.** `tab:app-localise`'s note restated the Bierens moment
as an inline display. It now names the paper's own numbered equation — "the $L^2(\Pi_u\otimes\Pi_t)$
norm of the sample analogue of \eqref{eq:Mdef} at cell $l$" — which is shorter, ties the diagnostic
to `def:operator` rather than paraphrasing it, and removes an inline formula from a float note,
where formulas drive the re-breaking this operation has to watch. `eq:Mdef` was confirmed to be a
live label in the article (`main.aux`: `newlabel{eq:Mdef}{{21}{38}}`) before the reference was
written, not assumed.

#### 28.13.4 A stale prose back-reference, found while compressing and repaired

`fig:app-phi`'s note read: "the two track each other to within $0.0049$ log points everywhere on the
grid, **which is the absence of shrinkage discussed in the text**."

**The text discusses no such thing.** The sentence it pointed at — "What the record does show is
that the width is not the footprint of shrinkage", at
`section6_verbatim.qmd:678` — was cut with the rest of §6.3 on 2026-08-27. `grep -n shrinkage
main.qmd` returned exactly one hit, the note's own back-reference. It has been dangling for a day
and would have shipped.

**Nothing in this portfolio could see it.** It names no label, no float and no number, so `\cref`
has nothing to resolve, the caption census sees no hole, and `render.sh`'s xdoc resolver — which now
matches five pointer forms including bare and compound — matches none of them, because there is no
ordinal in it at all. **A prose back-reference is a pointer with no check behind it.** This is the
second class of unguarded pointer the §6 cut has produced, after class 10 (§28.5), and unlike class
10 it is not machine-decidable: "discussed in the text" has no target a regex could resolve even in
principle. The standing defence is that **any pass that deletes prose must grep the float notes for
deictic back-references to it** ("discussed in the text", "as the text notes", "described above").

Repair: the measured fact is kept ($0.0049$ log points), the claim that the text discusses it is
gone. Confirmed absent from the printed PDF (`pdftotext | grep -c 'absence of shrinkage'` $\to0$;
the two remaining source hits are the comment blocks recording this finding, one the
`<!-- -->` §6 header block and one the `%` block above the figure).

#### 28.13.5 Float geometry re-measured, and the method does not rely on canaries

`tab:app-theta`'s block carried a certificate reading "38.15pt over with 34.12pt clearance" for a
float that landed at $77$pt. **No inherited certificate was trusted.** Heights were re-derived from
the rendered PDF with `pdftotext -bbox`, which gives the inked bottom edge directly:

$$\text{overrun}=y_{\max}(\text{last word})-720\,\text{bp},\qquad
  \text{clearance}=792\,\text{bp}-y_{\max}(\text{last word}),$$

the text block ending at $720$bp and the sheet at $792$bp, so $72.27$pt of overrun is exactly zero
clearance — the wall. **The method is validated against LaTeX's own arithmetic:** the same script
reports $12.50$pt for the one article float that does warn, and the log says
"Float too large for page by $12.49736$pt".

| Float | page | bottom edge (bp) | overrun before | overrun after | clearance after | gained |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `tab:app-firststage` | $104$ | $619.4$ | $-53.02$pt | $-101.02$pt | $173.29$pt | $+48.00$pt |
| `tab:app-localise` | $105$ | $371.3$ | $-109.37$pt | $-349.96$pt | $422.23$pt | $+240.59$pt |
| `tab:app-theta` | $107$ | $616.0$ | $-23.68$pt | $-104.43$pt | $176.70$pt | $+80.75$pt |
| `fig:app-phi` | $109$ | $545.3$ | $-82.50$pt | $-175.35$pt | $247.62$pt | $+92.85$pt |

A negative overrun is room above the bottom text margin. **Every float re-broke shorter, none
taller** — the failure mode the brief warned about (37 characters shorter, 10pt taller) did not
fire. `tab:app-theta` was the tightest float in the article at $95.95$pt of clearance and is now at
$176.70$pt.

**The `\scriptsize` on `tab:app-theta`'s notes is retained.** The 2026-08-20 repair is no longer
load-bearing at $135$ words, but restoring `\footnotesize` would spend most of what this pass
bought, and that float has already shed its Source line once.

A **global** scan was run as well, not just the four watched floats: every page of both documents,
maximum inked $y$ excluding the centred `fancyhdr` footer. Main's worst is page $96$ at $12.50$pt
($59.77$pt of clearance), the untouched Monte Carlo table, unchanged from the baseline. Nothing else
in the article exceeds $3.76$pt. **A watched list goes stale; the global scan needs no list.**
